To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a generalized method exists for evaluating the performance for any arbitrary sample rate conversion system, that the generalized method is valid for any single- and multicarrier modulation signal, that the generalized metric can be used for both single-carrier and multi-carrier signals, and that the generalized metric is valid for both fixed and variable fractional delay processing.
a VFD-ARSC design can be evaluated using a high performance filterbank, and the performance of the filterbank can be measured by the frequency-domain magnitude- (and phase-) error metrics.
the performance of any arbitrary sample rate conversion system can be evaluated by a generalized technique using a filter bank followed by magnitude and group delay error metrics.

the design and performance of VFD-ASR systems.
the design and evaluation of VFD-ASCR systems for digital signals.
the development of a method to assess the performance of VFD-ASR systems.

the generalized method proposed in this thesis can be used to determine the quality of any VFD ASRC design.
this work has provided a generalized method to evaluate the performance of any variable fractional delay arbitrary sample rate conversion design.
this work has provided the means by which any design for VFD- ASRC may be evaluated in a generalized fashion and compared to any other designs.

the generalized performance metric can be used to evaluate the performance of any design for VFD- ASRC.

the performance of any given VFD-ASR system is dependent on the input signal and the design parameters of the system.
a VFD- ASRC system should have a high performance filterbank and should be designed for the highest quality possible for the application.
